why: Substring printing with bounds checks; start/stop compared against len after conversion to size_t, so valid input has defined behavior.
Theme is a static running total; only possible signed overflow for huge strides is an ordinary error case.
Case is built around pow setting errno to EDOM/ERANGE, and whether math functions report errors via errno depends on implementation-defined math_errhandling.
Juliet-style bad() writes buffer[data] with an unchecked stdin index, so out-of-range input is an intended out-of-bounds write.
Named integer overflow: data+1 stored back into plain char, whose signedness and out-of-range conversion result are implementation-defined and are printed in hex.
bad() path (input 0) passes an uninitialized pointer to printLine, the explicit purpose of the case.
bad() path returns and then reads a pointer to an automatic array whose lifetime has ended.
bad() divides by user float that may be 0 and casts the resulting inf/huge value to int, the stated purpose of the case.
bad() stores CHAR_MAX*2 into char, an out-of-range conversion whose result (and char signedness) is implementation-defined and printed.
Exercises div() quotient/remainder, defined for ordinary inputs; div by zero or INT_MIN/-1 would be UB (7.22.6.2p2) only as an input error.
Struct mutation with strtol/errno-checked parsing; defined for valid input apart from ordinary overflow on extreme values.
Static struct mutation printed twice; defined behavior on valid input.
Static struct plus errno-checked strtol parsing; defined on valid input.
goto-based error handling with a static int read via scanf; fully defined.
Prints raw isalnum/isalpha/... return values whose nonzero value is left to the implementation, and passes a possibly negative char (UB) for non-ASCII bytes.
Counts characters with strchr; defined unless input fills all 1000 bytes without a terminator (ordinary error).
strcspn on two input lines; s[strlen-1] on an empty line would be UB only for malformed input.
Aliased out/in pointers without restrict are well defined in C; only ordinary signed overflow for large inputs.
restrict out pointer used with genuinely disjoint VLAs, so the restrict contract holds; defined.
Values assigned to unsigned and _Bool bit-fields are reduced/converted by defined rules and printed by member, not by layout.
Prints the object representation bytes of an int, whose byte order and representation are implementation-defined.
Prints the object representation bytes of a float, whose encoding and byte order are implementation-defined.
Hex-dumps a whole struct: endianness/float encoding implementation-defined and any padding bytes unspecified.
memcpy of an int into a char array then hex dump; output is the implementation-defined object representation.
memcpy of a float into bytes then hex dump; output is the implementation-defined float representation.
memcpy of a struct into bytes then hex dump; byte order implementation-defined and padding bytes unspecified.
auto storage class with 2*x+300; defined except ordinary signed overflow for extreme input.
register storage class with 2*x+300; defined except ordinary signed overflow for extreme input.
Type-puns a double through a union and prints the uint64 bits (implementation-defined representation), with %llx for uint64_t and %a formatting choices.
Theme is iso646 macros and digraph syntax; x | ~y depends on signed representation (6.2.6.2p2) only incidentally.

Underhanded C entry exploiting scanf semantics (stale buffers on partial matches); every line reads %d into an unsigned int* and buffers may be used uninitialized, but the hidden trick may be defined behavior.
Exercises nested macro expansion and token pasting; arithmetic is defined for ordinary arguments.
Buffer operations using non-overlapping memcpy with length checks; defined on valid input.
Buffer transforms using memmove, which is defined for overlapping regions; length capped at 256.

Theme is shared ownership via refcounts, but deleting a refcount-1 node frees it while the graph keeps the pointer, so a valid menu sequence (delete then show/exit) reaches use-after-free/double free.
The compare/compareN commands print the raw strcmp/strncmp result, for which only the sign is specified; the time command also prints the current time.
Code is explicitly marked VULNERABLE: strcmp on caller-supplied byte buffers not guaranteed to be NUL-terminated, plus unsigned wrap in text_len - pattern_len, giving out-of-bounds reads.
cute_c2 float collision tests on correctly typed structs; defined.
minimp3 dequantization; oversized shifts/reads only for bit-allocation values that are invalid in real streams.
Swaps pixel rows; defined for consistent w/h/buffer.
Float alpha premultiply with in-range float to uint8 conversions; defined.
minimp3 side-info parsing; out-of-range table index only for reserved header values (malformed input).
Float eigenvalue arithmetic with sqrtf clamped at 0; defined.
Bounded wide-string concat returning error codes; defined (reusing the reserved name wcscat is incidental).
Library form of errno_pow: behavior hinges on pow reporting EDOM/ERANGE via errno, which depends on implementation-defined math_errhandling.

bad(badData) divides by a caller float that may be 0 and converts the result to int, the stated purpose.
bad() stores CHAR_MAX*2 into char; out-of-range conversion and char signedness are implementation-defined.
Finds the minimum in a 3-node stack-allocated list; defined.
restrict used on genuinely disjoint VLAs, input parsed with sscanf; defined.
Base64 decode after filtering to ASCII alphabet chars; defined.
cute_c2 raycasts in float arithmetic (IEEE inf/NaN on degenerate input); defined.

cute_c2 manifold computation on correctly typed shapes; defined float logic.

Organic DEFLATE decoder whose normal path reads input bytes as uint32_t words (byte order implementation-defined, effective-type aliasing), though the case is not designed around this.
String search/replace with realloc; defined for non-empty search strings.
UTF-8 validation; the (char)0xC2-style conversions are implementation-defined but give the same result for signed or unsigned char.
Mode-based demos (uint16 range, memchr, malloc, function pointers); defined apart from ordinary overflow.
Shift-themed: left-shifts possibly negative values (UB), right-shifts negatives (implementation-defined), and checksums the int byte representation.
Struct/lookup operations with bounds checks; defined on valid input.
Theme is switch fallthrough and octal constants; output does not depend on the incidental ptr-- one past the start in process_array_reverse (6.5.6p8).
